record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Lower bound for plane spanning ratio
record.original_question: Determine the best possible universal lower bound on the spanning ratio of plane geometric graphs. More specifically, does there exist a real number t greater than √2.005367532 and a finite planar point set P such that every triangulation of P has spanning ratio at least t?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1. What is the best lower bound on the spanning ratio of plane geometric graphs? Specifically, is there a t > √2.005367532 and a point set P, such that every triangulation of P has spanning ratio at least t?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite point set P in the Euclidean plane, a triangulation of P is a maximal plane straight-line graph whose vertex set is P. For a plane straight-line graph G with vertex set P, the spanning ratio (stretch factor, or dilation) of G is

  sr(G) = max_{u,v ∈ P, u ≠ v} d_G(u,v) / |uv|,

where d_G(u,v) is the length of a shortest path from u to v in G (edges weighted by Euclidean length) and |uv| is the Euclidean distance. For a finite point set P, let

  τ(P) = inf { sr(T) : T is a triangulation of P },

and define the universal lower bound

  t* = sup_P τ(P),

where the supremum is taken over all finite planar point sets P.

It is known that t* ≥ √2.005367532. Determine the exact value of t*. In particular, decide whether there exists a real number t > √2.005367532 and a finite planar point set P such that every triangulation of P has spanning ratio at least t.
artifact.status_search_result: The best known universal lower bound for the spanning ratio of plane geometric graphs/triangulations remains close to √2.005367532 ≈ 1.4161. Subsequent work by Dumitrescu and Ghosh (2016) raised the lower bound for general plane spanners to 1.4308 using a 23-point configuration, but for triangulations specifically the question of whether the bound can be strictly improved above √2.005367532 does not appear to have been resolved in the recent literature, and the exact value of the supremum remains unknown.

status_evidence.title: Lower Bounds on the Dilation of Plane Spanners
status_evidence.snippet: Dumitrescu and Ghosh exhibited a 23-point set with dilation at least 1.4308, improving the previously best lower bound of 1.4161 for the worst-case dilation of plane spanners.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bounds on plane spanner dilation have been improved for general plane spanners, but the triangulation-specific bound √2.005367532 ≈ 1.4161 has not been demonstrably surpassed.

status_evidence.title: On plane geometric spanners: A survey and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing as open problem the question of improving the lower bound on the spanning ratio of plane geometric graphs above √2.005367532.
status_evidence.claim: The question is stated as an open problem in the geometric spanners survey literature.
